transcript.text: my washin mashine wont turn on at all no lights nothin

If your washing machine has absolutely no lights or display at all, the most common cause is simply that it isn't getting power from the wall. This could be a dead socket, a switched spur (a small switch on a fuse box or nearby plate) that's been turned off, or even just the plug having worked loose over time. Please try this simple check:
1. Unplug the washing machine.
2. Plug in a lamp or phone charger into that same socket.
3. Turn it on. Does it work?
4. Check if there is any separate switch controlling that socket and make sure it's on. If the lamp/charger doesn't work, the problem is with your home's electrical supply to that point (you'll need an electrician). If they do work, then the machine itself isn't receiving power despite a good socket, and we can look at the next likely cause.

i cant unplug it, its built in behind a cupboard door and im not allowed to take it out. the kettle works fine tho. i did look for a switch and theres a row of them above the worktop, the one saying 'washer' is off. my flatmate must of turned it off when cleaning

That explains it perfectly. The washing machine isn't getting power because the dedicated switch for it is turned off. Please turn that 'washer' switch back on. If turning the switch on doesn't make any difference, or if you hear a buzzing sound but nothing happens, let me know - but in most cases like this, simply switching it back on is all that's needed.
i switched it back on and its working now, the lights came on and everything. thanks!

Glad to hear it's working again. It was just the dedicated switch being turned off - a very common thing when cleaning or moving things around. To stop this from happening again, you might want to put a small sticky label on that 'washer' switch so you know which one it is next time. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

candidates: No power from the wall socket (dead socket, switched spur off, or loose plug) (high)
Faulty mains interference filter inside the machine (low)
